title: Self-Correction for Human Parsing
mechanism: Cyclic learning rate; at each cycle end, model weights are averaged into a running average and labels are replaced by a running average of label and model prediction, so model and labels improve together on ambiguous boundaries.
adaptation: All 24 classes: gridline (recall 0.33), splice (never predicted), edge_dark, material have boundary and missing-label noise. Five cosine cycles of 4k steps inside the 20k budget; label update only within 2 px of crack labels and on class boundaries so rare inactive is not erased. The weight averaging doubles as an EMA/SWA test.
min_experiment: Arm: 5-cycle self-correction, 5 seeds; baseline: house. Metrics: mIoU_rob, gridline IoU, crack relF1@2. Kill if mIoU_rob gain < 0.01 and gridline gain < 0.03.
evidence: R: human parsing benchmarks (LIP etc.); numbers not read here (abstract-level).
prior_overlap: partial: Mean Teacher pseudo-labels on unlabelled pools were run, but never correction of the labelled set's own labels; EMA/SWA never varied (BRIEF section 5).
